gateway_deploy_docker_intro: Drop the docker-compose.yml and gateway.env into a folder on your Synology / Linux host, then run 'docker compose up -d' (or use Synology Container Manager → Project → Create).
gateway_deploy_docker_intro_synology: Pick the Synology/NAS profile below, download both files, and follow the DSM 7.2+ click-through steps. Container Manager will pull the image and start the gateway.
gateway_deploy_docker_intro_linux: Pick the Linux profile below, download both files into a folder on your host (e.g. /opt/gatecontrol-gateway/), and run 'docker compose up -d'. systemd starts the container on boot via Docker's restart policy.
gateway_deploy_docker_platform_synology: Synology DSM / NAS / Docker Desktop (userspace WireGuard)
gateway_deploy_docker_platform_hint_syno: Synology DSM doesn't allow custom kernel modules, so wg-quick falls back to the wireguard-go userspace daemon. We bind-mount /dev/net/tun for it. Same applies to BSD-based NAS systems and Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows. ~2-3x slower than kernel WG but in practice unnoticeable for typical home use.
gateway_deploy_docker_platform_hint_linu: Standard Linux distributions ship the WireGuard kernel module since kernel 5.6 (Debian 11+, Ubuntu 22.04+, Fedora, etc.). Kernel WG uses netlink directly — no TUN device, no userspace daemon, full link-rate performance.
gateway_deploy_docker_net_hint_host: Host mode supports L4 routes (raw TCP) and Wake-on-LAN. Required for the full feature set. Watch out for port conflicts on the NAS host (8080, 9876, plus any L4 listen ports).
gateway_deploy_docker_net_hint_bridge: Bridge mode isolates the container but disables L4-route dynamic ports and breaks Wake-on-LAN multicast. Pick this only if your host blocks network_mode: host.
gateway_deploy_docker_synology_step1: Open File Station → /docker (create the folder if it doesn't exist) → create a subfolder named gatecontrol-gateway, then inside it another subfolder named config.
gateway_deploy_docker_synology_step2: Inside config/ create a text file named gateway.env and paste the gateway.env content from above.
gateway_deploy_docker_synology_step4: Project name: gatecontrol-gateway. Path: /docker/gatecontrol-gateway. Source: 'Create docker-compose.yml' — paste the docker-compose.yml content from above.
gateway_deploy_docker_synology_step5: Click Next, accept defaults, then Build. DSM pulls the image and starts the container.
gateway_deploy_docker_synology_step6: The gateway should appear as 'online' in this dashboard within ~30 seconds.
gateway_deploy_docker_linux_step1: SSH to your Linux host as root or a user in the docker group.
gateway_deploy_docker_linux_step3: Save the docker-compose.yml from above as /opt/gatecontrol-gateway/docker-compose.yml.
gateway_deploy_docker_linux_step4: Save gateway.env as /opt/gatecontrol-gateway/config/gateway.env, then chmod 600 on it (it contains the WireGuard private key).
gateway_deploy_docker_linux_step5: Start the container:  cd /opt/gatecontrol-gateway && docker compose up -d   — Docker pulls the image and starts the service.
gateway_deploy_docker_linux_step6: Watch the logs with 'docker compose logs -f' until you see 'Gateway running'. The peer should appear as 'online' in this dashboard within ~30 seconds.

waf.title: Web Application Firewall
waf.editor_desc: Inspects requests with the OWASP Core Rule Set (Coraza) before they reach the target.
waf.mode_detect_hint: Hits are only logged; no request is rejected.
waf.paranoia_1_hint: Baseline protection with few false positives – right for most applications.
waf.paranoia_2_hint: Additional rules against more sophisticated attacks; occasional false positives.
waf.paranoia_3_hint: Strict inspection; false positives are common and need exclusions.
waf.paranoia_4_hint: Very strict, only for especially sensitive applications; many exclusions needed.
waf.recommendation: Recommendation: run "Detect only" for 1–2 days first, review the events, exclude false positives, then switch to "Block".
waf.hint_http: The WAF is only available for HTTP entries.
waf.exclusions_hint: Exclusions apply immediately. The quickest way to add them is from the event list.
waf.tag_hint: Web Application Firewall: {{mode}}, paranoia level {{paranoia}} – click to edit
waf.err.invalid_rule: The rule ID must be a whole number between 1 and 9999999 (e.g. 942100).
waf.err.invalid_path: The path must start with / and must not contain spaces, quotes or backslashes (at most 256 characters).
waf.err.paranoia_invalid: The paranoia level must be between 1 and 4.
waf.err.requires_http: The WAF is only available for HTTP entries.
waf.err.license: The Web Application Firewall requires the Pro license.
waf.err.exclusion_limit: Too many exclusions for this route (at most 200 rules and 50 paths).
waf.err.filter_invalid: Invalid filter for the event list.

waf.asst_ready_hint: No false positives found – the entry can block.
waf.asst_review_hint: At least one rule hits normal users. Apply the suggested exclusions first, then block.
waf.asst_too_early_hint: Observed for less than 24 hours – wait a little longer.
waf.asst_no_traffic_hint: No request since the switch – without traffic nothing can be judged.

waf.trusted_desc: Addresses and networks that belong to you (home line, office, VPN). They never count in tiles, statistics and the assistant and are never banned.
waf.trusted_invalid: "{{value}}" is neither an IPv4/IPv6 address nor a CIDR network.
waf.bypass_label: Switch off the WAF for own IPs
waf.bypass_desc: Requests from own IPs are then not inspected at all – only useful if the WAF gets in the way of your own work.
waf.bypass_warn: Caution: if a listed address is shared (mobile network, company NAT, guest Wi-Fi) or later assigned to someone else, that stranger is exempt from the WAF too.
waf.bypass_confirm_title: Switch off the WAF for own IPs?
waf.bypass_confirm: Requests from {{n}} listed addresses or networks are no longer inspected after saving.
waf.autoban_desc: Bans an address on all HTTP entries when it triggers enough hits of the scanner rules within the time window (913 scanner, 930 file access, 931 remote include, 920440 restricted file extension). Own and private addresses are never banned.
waf.autoban_summary: Ban after {{threshold}} hits within {{window}} minutes for {{duration}} hours.
waf.bans_add_hint: The ban applies to all HTTP entries (answer 403). Networks at most /16 (IPv4) or /32 (IPv6); own IPs are never banned.
waf.err.trusted_invalid: At least one own IP is not a valid address or CIDR network (at most 50 entries).
waf.err.autoban_invalid: Hits 1–1000, time window 1–1440 minutes, ban duration 1–8760 hours.
waf.err.ban_ip_invalid: Invalid address. Networks at most /16 (IPv4) or /32 (IPv6); loopback is not possible.
waf.err.ban_trusted: This is an own IP – own IPs are never banned.
waf.err.token_forbidden: Only possible when signed in with the browser, not with an API token.
